# 1. Pagel's λ for milkweed-clade use

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ape)
library(phytools)
```

```{r}
plant_butterfly_long_all = read.csv("./plant_butterfly_long_all.csv")
```

-   We quantified phylogenetic signal in milkweed-clade association using Pagel’s λ (Pagel 1999).

-   Milkweed use was coded as a binary trait per species:

    -   `1` = recorded host use of the monophyletic milkweed clade (Asclepiadoideae + Secamonoideae)

    -   `0` = no recorded association

-   Pagel’s λ evaluates whether similarity in this trait among species is explained by shared evolutionary history

    -   Diagonal elements represent the total evolutionary variance accumulated along each lineage (root-to-tip branch length)

    -   Off-diagonal elements represent the shared branch length between species (shared ancestry).

-   Pagel’s λ rescales the internal branch lengths of the tree:

    -   λ = 0 → internal branches collapse; species are treated as independent (no phylogenetic signal)

    -   λ = 1 → full phylogenetic covariance retained; trait variation follows Brownian expectations.

    -   0 \< λ \< 1 → partial phylogenetic structuring.

-   The maximum-likelihood estimate of λ was obtained and compared to a model with λ constrained to 0 using a likelihood-ratio test.

-   A significant likelihood-ratio test indicates that milkweed association is phylogenetically conserved rather than randomly distributed across Danaini.

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Phylogenetic signal (Pagel’s λ) for milkweed-clade use
#
# Goal:
# Test whether use of the milkweed clade
# (Asclepiadoideae + Secamonoideae) is phylogenetically conserved
# across Danaini butterflies.
#
# Trait definition:
# milkweed = 1 → species has ≥1 host record in milkweed clade
# milkweed = 0 → no recorded association
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper function: standardize species names
# Ensures identical formatting between tree tips and dataset
# (removes whitespace inconsistencies that break joins)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
to_tip = function(x){
  x %>%
    as.character() %>%                 # ensure character type
    stringr::str_trim() %>%            # remove leading/trailing spaces
    stringr::str_replace_all("\\s+", "_")  # replace spaces with underscores
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Read Danaini phylogeny
# ------------------------------------------------------------
tree0 = ape::read.tree("./danaini_species_final_tree.newick")

# Standardize tree tip labels to match data formatting
tree0$tip.label = to_tip(tree0$tip.label)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Define focal milkweed clade (monophyletic  Apocynaceae lineage)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
milkweed_subfams = c("Asclepiadoideae", "Secamonoideae")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Build species-level binary trait
#
# From long host-record table:
# collapse multiple plant records per butterfly species
# into a single presence/absence value
# ------------------------------------------------------------
trait_df = plant_butterfly_long_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    butterfly_species = to_tip(butterfly_species),   # match tree labels
    plant_subfamily   = stringr::str_trim(as.character(plant_subfamily)),
    
    # ensure presence column behaves numerically
    # suppress warnings if NAs exist
    present_i = suppressWarnings(as.integer(present))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(butterfly_species) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    
    # milkweed = 1 if ANY host belongs to milkweed clade
    milkweed = as.integer(
      any(present_i == 1L &
          plant_subfamily %in% milkweed_subfams)
    ),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensure every tree species has a trait value
#
# Species absent from host database are coded as 0
# (= no recorded milkweed association)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
trait_full = tibble::tibble(
  butterfly_species = tree0$tip.label
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(trait_df, by = "butterfly_species") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    milkweed = tidyr::replace_na(milkweed, 0L)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Convert to named vector required by phytools
# Names MUST equal tree tip labels
# ------------------------------------------------------------
milkweed_vec = trait_full$milkweed
names(milkweed_vec) = trait_full$butterfly_species

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Enforce identical ordering between trait vector and tree
# (critical for comparative methods)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
milkweed_vec = milkweed_vec[tree0$tip.label]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Estimate Pagel’s λ
#
# λ measures how strongly trait similarity follows
# phylogenetic relatedness.
#
# λ = 0 → no phylogenetic signal
# λ = 1 → Brownian-motion expectation
#
# test = TRUE performs likelihood-ratio test vs λ = 0
# ------------------------------------------------------------
fit_lambda = phytools::phylosig(
  tree   = tree0,
  x      = milkweed_vec,
  method = "lambda",
  test   = TRUE
)

# Display results
fit_lambda
```
